purpose: Refs that repository branch hygiene must never delete. They either hold durable provider state or are content-addressed evidence that runtime bindings and operational documents reference by name.
deletion_rule: A ref listed here is not a work branch, so neither age, nor a zero-ahead comparison against main, nor byte-identical duplication makes it deletable. Deleting one breaks a live binding: on 2026-10-21 the ref agent/milovi-video-accepted-73c578eff825 was deleted as a byte-identical duplicate and had to be restored, because the Milovi sendVideo binding, the workflow contract and current-state all name it. Any cleanup must read this file first, and tests/test_milovi_evidence_binding.py fails if a listed ref appears in a deletion ledger.

refs.why: Verified LordChrist publication ledger, dispatch intents and results. The publisher reads and advances it; the exact tip is evidence, not an invariant.
Milovi Telegram feed ledger; losing it would destroy provider-effect history and duplicate-suppression state.
Svodka publication ledger; the historical 14-entry ledger is terminal no-replay evidence.

Artifact store for the 16 accepted Milovi Telegram videos. The ref name is the prefix of the accepted evidence digest sha256:73c578eff82563..., and the runtime constant milovi_telegram_feed.VIDEO_ARTIFACT_REF binds sendVideo to it. The 16 MP4 blobs on the ref are exactly the git_blob_sha1 values recorded in content/telegram/milovi-cake/accepted-video-reservoir-2026-08.json.

Later re-materialization of the same 16 videos: every artifact blob is byte-identical to the accepted ref, and only the evidence generation differs (identity sha256:f0e25d9c905fc95... versus the accepted sha256:73c578eff8256...). No code references it, so it proves reproducibility rather than binding a release.
